hero.title: Hīnayāna and its Historical Decline
hero.description: An analytical study of the early conservative school of Buddhism, its doctrinal rigidity, and the systemic causes that led to its decline in ancient India.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Tenets

  • Focus on individual salvation (Arhat ideal).
  • Rejection of Bodhisattva concept.
  • Literal interpretation of Pali Canon.

Key Sects

  • Sthaviravada (Elders).
  • Sarvastivada.
  • Pudgalavada.
  • Causes of Decline:
    • Royal Patronage Shift: The rise of Mahayana, supported by Gupta and Pala rulers, reduced Hīnayāna influence.
    • Doctrinal Rigidity: Inability to adapt to mass appeal compared to the bhakti-oriented Mahayana.
    • Language Barrier: Persistent use of Pali vs. the rising popularity of Sanskrit-based Mahayana texts.
    • Foreign Invasions: Hūṇa invasions targeted monasteries; the decentralised Hīnayāna structure lacked resilience.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Key milestones marking the transition of the Hīnayāna sect from dominance to marginalization.

cards.details: Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali; the split between Sthaviravada (precursor to Hīnayāna) and Mahasanghika.
Fourth Buddhist Council under Kanishka; formalization of the Sarvastivada school, often associated with early Hīnayāna trends.
Xuanzang visits India; documents the coexistence of Hīnayāna and Mahayana monasteries, noting the growing dominance of the latter.

items.title: S.T.A.R.S
items.decryption: Core components of Hīnayāna: Sthaviravada roots, Theravada tradition, reliance on Abhidharma, doctrinal rigidity, and focus on individual salvation.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Thinking Hīnayāna was eradicated entirely; it survived in Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, and parts of the Indian subcontinent.
Confusing Hīnayāna with Mahayana deities; Hīnayāna treats Buddha as a human teacher, not a divine savior.
Assuming Hīnayāna is the same as early Buddhism; it is a specialized nomenclature that evolved over time.
